_read_this_first: Every row here is a migration file that RECORDS SQL production had already executed, recovered byte-exact from supabase_migrations.schema_migrations.statements. A row is not a pardon and it is not a bypass flag: scripts/ci/recording-only.mjs accepts it only when the file on disk hashes to `md5`, and scripts/ci/check-recorded-migrations-evidence.mjs then asks production whether that same md5 is what public.fn_ca_migration_text(version) returns for that version and whether each finding the file-text guards raised is still true of the live schema. A genuinely new migration cannot be made to hash to a version production already has, which is what stops this file being used to get new work past a guard. Adding a row without the live evidence turns the `Applied Migrations Are Recorded` workflow red and files an issue.
_how_to_add_a_row: 1. Recover the file: SELECT array_to_string(statements, chr(10)) FROM supabase_migrations.schema_migrations WHERE version='<v>'. Write those bytes and NOTHING else: no header, and no newline the database does not already have. 2. Prove it: md5 of the file must equal the md5 column of public.fn_ca_migration_text('<v>'). 3. Read every finding the guards raise against PRODUCTION and write what you found in `liveVerdict` - the grants, the register row, the register entry - not what you expect. 4. If a finding is still TRUE of production, fix production first. The recording is not the place to settle it.

TO anon,authenticated,service_role, it is SECURITY DEFINER, and it never calls auth.uid(). Closed in production on 2026-09-19 07:13:57Z by migration 20260919071357 anon_grant_from_public_is_the_one_that_mattered, so the exposure ran 2 days 19 hours 58 minutes. Read live 2026-09-23: proacl is {postgres=X/postgres,authenticated=X/postgres,service_role=X/postgres}, has_function_privilege('anon',...) is false. It is STABLE and read-only, takes two uuids the caller must already know, and is the qual of RLS policy personal_notification_destination on public.notifications, so EXECUTE for authenticated must stay: revoking it would deny every SELECT on notifications to every logged-in player.
